intended_object: Given a Hecke pair (Δ, H) and elements g, β ∈ Δ, write the double coset as a disjoint union HgH = ⊔ᵢ σᵢgH. The definition is meant to give the finite set of left cosets {βσᵢgH}, which is the same as the set of left H-cosets contained in βHgH. This is the support of the image of the basis element [βH] under right multiplication by [HgH] (Shimura §3.1). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the image of the finite index type `DecompQuotient H H g` under the map i ↦ (β·σᵢ·g)H, where σᵢ = `i.out` ∈ H. The result lives in `HeckeCoset Δ ⊥ H`; the library shows this type is exactly the left cosets βH with β ∈ Δ (`mk_bot_eq_mk_bot`). Here `DecompQuotient H H g` is the quotient H/(gHg⁻¹ ∩ H), and its representatives σᵢ give the standard decomposition HgH = ⊔ σᵢgH (`mk_out_mul_injective`).

The surrounding lemmas confirm the definition gives the right set:
- `mk_bot_mem_smulOrbit_iff`: ξH is in the orbit iff β⁻¹ξ ∈ HgH.
- `smulOrbit_congr` and `smulOrbit_congr_left`: the set depends only on the cosets βH and HgH, not on the choice of representatives.
- `smulOrbit_card`: the set has exactly [H : gHg⁻¹ ∩ H] elements.
- `smulOrbit_disjoint`: orbits of different double cosets are disjoint.

So the definition is exactly Shimura's set {βσᵢgH}. Under `[IsHeckeTriple Δ H H]` it is stated for an arbitrary group G, submonoid Δ and subgroup H, which is the natural setting for an abstract Hecke ring. That hypothesis is needed for the index set to be finite, so the set can be a `Finset`. Mathlib has no corresponding notion; Hecke rings are not in Mathlib.
